title: Reversal Payment on Dwelling Water Damage — HomeGuard Homeowners Policy Claims Manual
content:
**Clause.** On a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy claim, the reversal payment on the dwelling water damage is its covered amount, less the deductible it absorbs, less any dwelling money already issued on the claim; the result is never below 0.00 and is rounded to the cent once, on the final figure.

## 1. The claim and its figures

1.1 The claim concerned is the latest first-notice entry on the policy, whose recorded date of loss, report date and cause of loss govern this settlement.

1.2 The replacement-cost value and depreciation of the dwelling water damage are those recorded on its repeated-seepage denial entry.

1.3 The dwelling money already issued on the claim is the total of every dwelling payment entry of that claim.

## 2. The occurrence deductible

2.1 The occurrence deductible for the water loss is the all-other-perils deductible on the declarations, or for a wind or hail loss the larger of the declarations' wind and hail percentage of Coverage A and the tier's wind and hail deductible minimum.

2.2 Where the tier's deductible waiver threshold is above 0 and the replacement-cost values on the claim's denial entries and on its payment entries that replace no denial together reach it, no deductible applies to the dwelling water damage. "Reach" means equal to or above the threshold.

2.3 The deductible left for the dwelling water damage is the whole occurrence deductible.

2.4 When no waiver applies, the dwelling water damage absorbs the smaller of the deductible left for it and its covered amount.

## 3. The covered amount

3.1 The covered amount of the dwelling water damage is the full replacement-cost value when that value is at or below the tier's no-holdback threshold, and otherwise the replacement-cost value less the depreciation recognized.

3.2 The depreciation recognized is the depreciation recorded on the denial entry.

## 4. Assembly of the payment

| Line | Quantity |
|---|---|
| A | covered amount (section 3) |
| B | deductible absorbed (section 2) |
| C | dwelling money already issued on the claim (1.3) |
| Payment | A less B less C, rounded to the cent once on that final figure, and 0.00 if the figure falls below 0.00 |

The rounding is applied once, to the final figure, and never to an intermediate line.

## 5. Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

The inputs below are chosen for illustration only; they are not rates, limits or thresholds of any HomeGuard package.

**Example 5.1 — value above the no-holdback threshold.** Hypothetical inputs: replacement-cost value on the denial entry 12000.00; recorded depreciation 3000.00; no-holdback threshold 1000.00; all-other-perils deductible 1000.00; the tier's waiver threshold 0; no dwelling money issued.
- Covered amount: 12000.00 less 3000.00 gives 9000.00.
- Deductible absorbed: the smaller of 1000.00 and 9000.00, that is 1000.00.
- Payment: 9000.00 less 1000.00 less 0.00 gives 8000.00.

**Example 5.2 — value at the no-holdback threshold.** Hypothetical inputs: replacement-cost value 1000.00; recorded depreciation 250.00; no-holdback threshold 1000.00; all-other-perils deductible 500.00; no waiver; nothing issued. The value is at the threshold, so the covered amount is the full 1000.00; the deductible absorbed is 500.00; the payment is 500.00. At 1000.01 the covered amount would instead be 1000.01 less 250.00, that is 750.01, and the payment 250.01.

**Example 5.3 — covered amount below the deductible.** Hypothetical inputs: covered amount 400.00; deductible left 1000.00; no waiver; nothing issued. The deductible absorbed is 400.00, the smaller of the two, and the payment is 0.00.

**Example 5.4 — waiver reached.** Hypothetical inputs: the tier's waiver threshold 50000.00; replacement-cost values on the claim's denial entries and its payment entries that replace no denial totalling 50000.00; covered amount 30000.00; dwelling money already issued 2000.00. The total reaches the threshold, so no deductible applies and the payment is 30000.00 less 2000.00, that is 28000.00. Had the total been 49999.99, the deductible left would have been absorbed.

**Example 5.5 — money already issued exceeds the remainder.** Hypothetical inputs: covered amount 3000.00; deductible absorbed 1000.00; dwelling money already issued 2500.00. The figure 3000.00 less 1000.00 less 2500.00 falls below 0.00, so the payment is 0.00.

## 6. Points of judgement

- **Which cause of loss sets the deductible.** The cause recorded on the latest first-notice entry: a wind or hail cause takes the larger of the wind and hail percentage of Coverage A and the tier's wind and hail minimum; every other cause takes the all-other-perils deductible on the declarations.
- **Which figures are read from the denial.** The replacement-cost value and depreciation of the dwelling water damage come from its repeated-seepage denial entry on that claim, not from any estimate outside the claim file.
- **Which entries count toward the waiver.** Every denial entry of the claim together with every payment entry of the claim that replaces no denial.
